# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **“use at most the first three row selectors and the first three column selectors, then apply the command normally.”** Every labeled canonical input has at most three selectors on each axis, so this rival matches all five canonical outputs exactly.

An exact disagreement emitted by the repaired generator is seed 0, sample index 0, difficulty `easy`:

```json
[
  [1,8,0,0,8],
  [8,6,1,7,8],
  [8,5,9,3,2],
  [8,4,6,1,7],
  [8,8,5,9,3]
]
```

The intended rule sees four selected rows and columns 1 and 4, producing:

```json
[[6,8],[5,2],[4,7],[8,3]]
```

The first-three rival drops the fourth selected row and predicts:

```json
[[6,8],[5,2],[4,7]]
```

I checked the intended output with the supported canonical Racket application command. The retained report is `checks/counterexamples/66a121e0d7e4-first-three-racket.json`; it records executed rule hash `c03aadcd616e`, final generator SHA-256 `da201e9ac177acbd53a435c18b5c3d33fa1e86f06c3c1fb89d3353f3be041705`, input/output hashes, and the 4x2 output above. The independent Python oracle agrees.

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases routinely. Its default eight-step schedule gives every sample four selectors on at least one axis. In the independent 400-sample audit, the intended rule disagreed with this shortcut on 400/400 samples; the 300-lesson production census and all 2,400 query rotations found no surviving declared rival.
